title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten no-purchase outings on Georgetown’s campus and in nearby National Park Service spaces, with university or federal confirmation of free access.

cards.entity_name: Maria & Alberto de la Cruz Art Gallery
cards.title: Compare Notes at de la Cruz Gallery
cards.subtitle: A free contemporary-art hang inside Georgetown University
cards.notes: Bring a friend, view the current exhibition together, then trade observations about one work before leaving the gallery.
cards.short_summary: A conversation-ready campus art stop where exhibitions and programs carry no charge.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown University states that the Maria & Alberto de la Cruz Art Gallery is one of its two art-gallery venues and that all exhibitions and programs are free.
cards.source_title: Galleries | Department of Art and Art History | Georgetown University
cards.access_notes: All exhibitions and programs are free; consult the gallery page for current exhibition details and public visiting information.

cards.entity_name: Lucille M. & Richard F.X. Spagnuolo Art Gallery
cards.title: Take a Two-Person Gallery Break
cards.subtitle: Free exhibitions in Georgetown’s Spagnuolo Gallery
cards.notes: Meet between classes, choose one piece each to examine closely, and compare what caught your attention on the way out.
cards.short_summary: A compact, no-cost art meetup centered on Georgetown’s second named gallery venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown University identifies the Lucille M. & Richard F.X. Spagnuolo Art Gallery as an exhibition venue and says all gallery exhibitions and programs are free.
cards.source_title: Galleries | Department of Art and Art History | Georgetown University
cards.access_notes: All exhibitions and programs are free; verify current gallery access and exhibition dates before meeting.

cards.title: Browse Lauinger’s Community Exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Free public displays of Georgetown scholarship and creative work
cards.notes: Pick a current gallery display, walk through it with classmates, and use one object or caption to start a longer discussion.
cards.short_summary: Rotating campus displays turn a library meetup into a free shared viewing session.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgetown University Library says Lauinger’s community exhibitions showcase faculty, staff, and student work and are open to the public free of charge.
cards.source_title: Guidelines for Library Community Galleries | Georgetown University Library
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions are open to the public free of charge; non-Georgetown visitors should confirm current library entry procedures.

cards.title: Walk the Waterfront Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: A free riverside reset below campus
cards.notes: Start at the western-end labyrinth, walk its turns together, then continue along the car-free path for Potomac views.
cards.short_summary: A contemplative labyrinth and riverside walk combine into one purchase-free meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that all of Rock Creek Park is free to enter; Georgetown Waterfront Park is one of the Georgetown sites it manages.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter. Rock Creek Park outdoor areas are generally open during daylight hours; check NPS alerts before visiting.

cards.title: Follow the Woodland Paths at Dumbarton Oaks Park
cards.subtitle: A free historic-landscape walk northeast of campus
cards.notes: Enter the NPS-managed naturalistic park with friends, follow established paths, and pause at its stone-lined landscape features.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission woodland outing through Beatrix Farrand’s historic naturalistic landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service names Dumbarton Oaks Park among Rock Creek Park destinations and states that all of Rock Creek Park is free to enter.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter and intended for daylight use. Stay on established paths and distinguish this NPS park from the separately operated formal gardens.

cards.title: Bring a Picnic to Montrose Park
cards.subtitle: A free green-space meetup near Georgetown
cards.notes: Pack food from home, claim a picnic table or lawn spot, and add a walk past the Ropewalk and historic boxwood garden.
cards.short_summary: A casual, bring-your-own picnic framed by a sixteen-acre historic park landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that all of Rock Creek Park is free to enter; Montrose Park is a Rock Creek Park site overlooking Georgetown.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter during daylight hours. Bringing food from home keeps the hang purchase-free; permits may apply to organized group uses.

cards.title: Hike the Glover-Archbold Trail
cards.subtitle: A free wooded route west of Georgetown
cards.notes: Meet at a marked trail entrance, wear shoes suited to rugged dirt paths, and watch carefully at the park’s street crossings.
cards.short_summary: A nearly 2.5-mile woodland trail offers a free group walk within reach of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that all of Rock Creek Park is free to enter; Glover-Archbold Park is one of its managed park sites.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter during daylight hours. Paths are rugged and for foot traffic; use caution where the trail crosses streets.

cards.title: Meet in the Old Stone House Garden
cards.subtitle: A free historic stop on M Street
cards.notes: Start in the rear garden, then visit the open ground-floor exhibits together and compare details from the house’s long timeline.
cards.short_summary: Georgetown’s oldest structure and its garden provide a free history-focused meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service explicitly says Rock Creek Park and the Old Stone House are free to enter.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter. Grounds follow daylight hours, while interior access is limited to posted opening days and currently open areas.

cards.title: Cross Whitehaven Park Together
cards.subtitle: A free trail link between nearby park landscapes
cards.notes: Use the cross trail for a short group walk, carry water, and decide in advance whether to continue toward Glover-Archbold or Dumbarton Oaks Park.
cards.short_summary: A grassy and wooded connector supports an easy, no-purchase walking meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that all of Rock Creek Park is free to enter; Whitehaven Park is a Rock Creek Park unit near Georgetown.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter during daylight hours. Use established trails and check current NPS conditions before extending the walk into adjoining parks.

cards.title: Sketch the Francis Scott Key Memorial
cards.subtitle: A free outdoor drawing meetup beside the C&O Canal
cards.notes: Bring paper and pencils, choose a view of the bust or limestone pergola, and spend twenty minutes sketching before sharing results.
cards.short_summary: A named Georgetown memorial becomes a simple, supply-from-home creative hang.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that all of Rock Creek Park is free to enter; the Francis Scott Key Memorial is an NPS Rock Creek Park site.
cards.source_title: Basic Information - Rock Creek Park | U.S. National Park Service
cards.access_notes: Free to enter during daylight hours. Bring drawing materials from home so no purchase is required.
